Funding FAQs

How long does it take for deposits to be available?

Debit card deposits are typically available immediately. ACH transfers usually take 1-3 business days. Wire transfers received before 2 PM ET are generally available same day. Check deposits take 5-7 business days after receipt.

Are there any deposit fees?

Nadex does not charge any fees for deposits. However, your bank may charge fees for wire transfers or other services.

What is the minimum deposit?

The minimum initial deposit to open a Nadex account is $250. After your account is open, there is no minimum for subsequent deposits.

How do I request a withdrawal?

Log in to your Nadex account, go to the Account section, and select "Withdraw Funds." Follow the prompts to select your withdrawal method and amount.

Can I withdraw to a different bank account than the one I used to deposit?

For security and regulatory purposes, withdrawals must generally be returned to the original funding source. If you need to withdraw to a different account, please contact our customer support for assistance.

CFTC Regulation

Nedaxer is regulated by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), which oversees the US derivatives markets, including futures, options, and swaps. This regulation requires us to:

Segregated Funds

What Are Binary Options?

Binary options are limited-risk contracts based on a simple yes/no market proposition. For example, "Will EUR/USD be above 1.1050 at 3:00 PM ET?" If you buy this option and EUR/USD is above 1.1050 at 3:00 PM ET, your option settles at 100 and you receive the full payout. If EUR/USD is at or below 1.1050, the option settles at 0.

On Nadex, binary options trade between 0 and 100, representing the probability of the event occurring. Your maximum risk and potential profit are known before you place your trade.

Binary Option Basics

  • Binary options trade between 0 and 100
  • The price represents the probability of the event occurring
  • If you buy at 42.50, your maximum risk is $42.50 per contract
  • Your maximum potential profit is $57.50 per contract (100 - 42.50)
  • If your binary settles at 100, you receive the full $100 payout

Trading Binary Options

  • Buy if you think the statement will be true at expiration
  • Sell if you think the statement will be false at expiration
  • Close positions early to secure profits or limit losses

What Are Crypto Call Spreads?

Call spreads on Nedaxer are limited-risk alternatives to traditional cryptocurrency options, with built-in floor and ceiling levels. They provide a way to participate in crypto market movements with predefined risk and potential profit.

Unlike traditional crypto options, Nedaxer call spreads are fully collateralized, which means you always know your maximum potential loss and profit before placing your trade.

Benefits of Crypto Call Spreads

  • Limited risk with predefined maximum loss - perfect for volatile crypto markets
  • Defined profit potential with built-in ceiling for target-based trading
  • Lower cost compared to binary options in some cryptocurrency scenarios
  • Partial outcomes based on where crypto price settles in the range

How Crypto Call Spreads Work

  • Choose a cryptocurrency market and expiration time
  • Select a call spread with floor and ceiling price levels
  • Buy if you think the crypto will rise, sell if you think it will fall
  • Ability to close early to secure profits or limit losses during market swings

Sample Crypto Call Spread Trade

Bitcoin (BTC/USD) Example

In this example, you believe Bitcoin will rise from its current price of $65,500 but want protection against price drops.

  • Call Spread Range: $65,000 (floor) to $68,000 (ceiling)
  • Your Position: Buy at $1,500 per contract
  • Maximum Risk: $1,500 (your purchase price)
  • Maximum Reward: $1,500 (if BTC price is at or above $68,000 at expiration)

Outcome: If BTC reaches $67,000 at expiration, you earn $1,000 profit, even though it didn't reach the ceiling price.

Introduction to Forex Trading

The foreign exchange market (forex) is the largest financial market in the world, with daily trading volumes exceeding $6 trillion. Forex trading involves the simultaneous buying of one currency and selling of another, with traders speculating on the changing values between currency pairs.

Trading forex on Web Trading Platform offers unique advantages compared to traditional forex brokers. With binary options and call spreads, you can trade major and minor currency pairs with completely limited risk. This means you always know your maximum potential loss before entering a trade — a significant benefit in the highly volatile forex market.

Advantages of Trading Forex on Web Trading Platform

  • Defined and limited risk on every trade
  • No margin calls or leverage-related liquidations
  • Access to major and minor currency pairs
  • Multiple expiration timeframes from minutes to days
  • No need to calculate pip values or position sizing

Major Currency Pairs

Web Trading Platform offers trading on all major currency pairs, which feature the highest liquidity and typically the tightest spreads in the forex market.

Currency Pair Description Characteristics
EUR/USD Euro/US Dollar Most traded pair with highest liquidity; influenced by EU and US economic data
GBP/USD British Pound/US Dollar More volatile than EUR/USD; sensitive to UK politics and Brexit developments
USD/JPY US Dollar/Japanese Yen Often functions as a safe haven; sensitive to interest rate differentials
USD/CHF US Dollar/Swiss Franc Another safe-haven currency; often moves inversely to EUR/USD
AUD/USD Australian Dollar/US Dollar Commodity currency highly correlated with gold and Chinese economic data
USD/CAD US Dollar/Canadian Dollar Strongly influenced by oil prices and US-Canadian trade relations

Web Trading Platform also offers several minor currency pairs (cross-pairs) that don't include the USD, providing additional trading opportunities:

  • EUR/GBP (Euro/British Pound)
  • EUR/JPY (Euro/Japanese Yen)
  • GBP/JPY (British Pound/Japanese Yen)
  • AUD/JPY (Australian Dollar/Japanese Yen)
  • EUR/AUD (Euro/Australian Dollar)

Forex Market Drivers

Understanding what moves currency markets is essential for successful forex trading. Several key factors influence currency values:

Economic Indicators

Key economic data releases that significantly impact forex markets:

  • Non-Farm Payrolls (US)
  • GDP Growth Rates
  • Inflation Data (CPI, PPI)
  • Retail Sales
  • Manufacturing and Services PMIs
  • Consumer Confidence

Central Bank Policies

Central bank decisions and communications often create significant market movements:

  • Interest Rate Decisions
  • Quantitative Easing/Tightening Programs
  • Forward Guidance Statements
  • Press Conferences and Minutes

Geopolitical Events

Political developments that can drive currency volatility:

  • Elections and Regime Changes
  • Trade Agreements/Disputes
  • International Conflicts
  • Brexit-type Events

Economic Calendar Trading

Web Trading Platform products are particularly well-suited for trading around high-impact economic releases. With binary options, you can position for the expected market reaction without risking more than your initial investment, even during extreme volatility following major announcements.

Forex Trading Strategies

Several trading strategies work particularly well with Web Trading Platform's binary options and call spreads when applied to forex markets:

Trend Following with Binary Options

Using binary options to trade with established trends:

  • Identify the trend using moving averages (20, 50, 200-period)
  • Wait for pullbacks to support levels or moving averages
  • Enter a binary option in the direction of the trend
  • Select an expiration that allows enough time for the move to develop

Range Trading with Call Spreads

Using call spreads to capitalize on range-bound currency pairs:

  • Identify clear support and resistance levels on the chart
  • Buy call spreads near support levels
  • Set the floor near support and ceiling below resistance
  • Profit from the movement within the range while limiting risk

News Trading Strategies

Capitalizing on forex volatility around major economic releases:

  • Identify high-impact news events from economic calendars
  • Analyze the expected figures versus forecasts
  • Position with binary options shortly before the announcement
  • Use shorter expirations to capitalize on immediate market reactions

Strategy Example: Trading EUR/USD on NFP Release

  1. Review economists' consensus forecast for NFP
  2. Analyze recent EUR/USD technical setup
  3. If NFP comes in significantly higher than expected, US Dollar typically strengthens
  4. Position with a binary option predicting EUR/USD will be lower at expiration
  5. Choose a 1-hour expiration to capture the immediate market reaction
  6. Risk is limited to the premium paid for the binary option

Risk Management for Forex

While Web Trading Platform products have built-in risk management through limited maximum loss, implementing additional risk control measures is essential for long-term success:

Position Sizing

Limit each trade to 1-2% of your total trading capital. Even with defined-risk products, proper position sizing prevents large drawdowns from consecutive losses.

Correlation Awareness

Be mindful of correlations between currency pairs. Trading multiple correlated pairs in the same direction effectively increases your position size and risk exposure.

Time Management

Match your expiration selection to your analysis timeframe. For instance, don't use 5-minute binary options when trading based on daily chart patterns.

Risk Management Advantage

One of the primary advantages of trading forex with Web Trading Platform is the elimination of the unlimited risk typical with spot forex trading. No matter how volatile the currency pair becomes, your risk is always capped at your initial investment amount.

Introduction to Technical Analysis

Technical analysis is a methodology used by traders to evaluate securities and identify trading opportunities by analyzing statistical trends gathered from trading activity, such as price movement and volume. Unlike fundamental analysis, which looks at a company's business performance, technical analysis focuses exclusively on price charts and related indicators.

For traders on Web Trading Platform, technical analysis provides a framework for making decisions about when to enter and exit trades across all available products, including binary options, call spreads, and knock-outs. The limited-risk nature of these products makes them ideal for implementing technical analysis strategies.

Key Principles of Technical Analysis

  • Price discounts everything - all known information is reflected in the price
  • Price moves in trends - once established, trends are more likely to continue than reverse
  • History tends to repeat itself - market psychology often leads to recurring patterns

Chart Types and Patterns

Different chart types offer varying perspectives on price action. The Web Trading Platform offers several chart types for technical analysis:

Line Charts

The simplest form of chart, displaying only the closing prices connected by a line. Line charts provide a clean view of overall price movement but lack detail on intraday price fluctuations.

Bar Charts

Each bar represents a time period and shows the opening, high, low, and closing prices (OHLC). Bar charts provide more information than line charts while remaining visually uncluttered.

Candlestick Charts

Similar to bar charts but with a visual emphasis on the relationship between opening and closing prices. The "body" of the candle shows the range between open and close, while "wicks" show the high and low. Candlesticks are particularly useful for identifying short-term patterns.

Common Chart Patterns

Reversal Patterns

Signals that a trend may be about to change direction:

  • Head and Shoulders
  • Double Tops and Bottoms
  • Rounded Bottoms (Saucers)

Continuation Patterns

Indicates a pause in the trend before continuing in the same direction:

  • Flags and Pennants
  • Triangles (Ascending, Descending, Symmetrical)
  • Rectangles

Pattern Trading on Web Trading Platform

Chart patterns work especially well with binary options where you can position for specific price movement within a defined timeframe. For example, identifying a bullish flag pattern could present an excellent opportunity to enter a "Higher" binary option with the right expiration time.

Technical Indicators

Technical indicators are mathematical calculations based on price, volume, or open interest that aim to forecast financial market direction. The Web Trading Platform provides a comprehensive suite of indicators that can be applied to your charts.

Trend Indicators

Help identify the direction of the market:

  • Moving Averages (Simple, Exponential, Weighted)
  • Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD)
  • Average Directional Index (ADX)

Momentum Indicators

Identify the strength of price movement and potential reversal points:

  • Relative Strength Index (RSI)
  • Stochastic Oscillator
  • Commodity Channel Index (CCI)

Volatility Indicators

Measure the rate of price movement, regardless of direction:

  • Bollinger Bands
  • Average True Range (ATR)
  • Standard Deviation

Indicator Combinations for Better Results

Combining different types of indicators can provide confirmation and reduce false signals. For example, using a trend indicator (moving average) with a momentum indicator (RSI) can help identify high-probability trading opportunities when both signals align.

Support and Resistance

Support and resistance are key concepts in technical analysis that represent price levels where a market repeatedly tends to reverse direction.

Support Levels

Price levels where buying interest appears strong enough to overcome selling pressure, halting downward price movement. Support forms when prices stop falling and bounce higher.

Resistance Levels

Price levels where selling pressure appears strong enough to overcome buying pressure, halting upward price movement. Resistance forms when prices stop rising and fall back.

Support/Resistance Role Reversal

Once a support or resistance level is broken, its role often reverses. Former support becomes new resistance, and former resistance becomes new support.

Trading Support and Resistance on Web Trading Platform

Binary options and call spreads are ideal for trading at support and resistance levels. For example, buying a binary option at support with an expectation that the price will be higher at expiration, or placing a call spread with the floor near a support level to define your risk.

Application to Trading Products

Technical analysis can be applied to all Web Trading Platform products, each with unique advantages for different technical approaches.

Binary Options

Binary options are ideal for technical setups with clear directional bias and timeframes:

  • Trade reversals from support/resistance levels
  • Execute on momentum indicator signals
  • Position for breakouts from chart patterns

Call Spreads

Call spreads work well with technical analysis for range-bound markets:

  • Set floor and ceiling based on technical support/resistance
  • Capitalize on trends with defined risk parameters
  • Use volatility indicators to determine optimal spread width

Knock-Outs

Knock-Outs combine leverage with technical analysis for trending markets:

  • Place knockout levels beyond key technical levels
  • Use trend indicators to confirm direction
  • Align trade direction with longer-term technical trends

Technical Analysis Workflow

  1. Identify market condition (trending, ranging, volatile)
  2. Apply appropriate indicators for the condition
  3. Identify key support/resistance levels
  4. Select the appropriate product (binary option, call spread, or knock-out)
  5. Choose expiration time based on timeframe of your analysis
  6. Execute trade with defined risk parameters

Best Practices

  • Combine multiple timeframes for better perspective
  • Look for confirmation across different indicators
  • Use risk management with every trade
  • Journal your trades to review and improve your technical approach
